deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page: A is a von Neumann algebra and T is a positive (semifinite, normal) trace on it. The letters a and b denote two-sided ideals attached to T. The underlined a is probably the ideal of T-integrable elements; underlined b is probably a hereditary ideal containing it, plausibly the ideal of definition generated by projections of finite trace. Underlined c is a commutative subalgebra of b, assumed maximal, identified with C_0(M) by Gelfand theory. A bounded Borel function f on M gives an operator U_f in the weak closure of c.

Step 1 (Lemma). If |f| ≤ g with g in C_0(M), then 0 ≤ |U_f| ≤ U_g ∈ b. Since b is an ideal of a von Neumann algebra it is hereditary, so U_f ∈ b. By maximality of c, U_f = U_h for some h in C_0(M).

Step 2. Apply this to f = φ_k, the characteristic function of a compact set k ⊂ M. Then E = U_{φ_k} is a projection lying in c. So there is a compact open-closed set k' containing k with U_{φ_k} = U_{φ_{k'}}. This reflects the (locally) hyperstonean nature of M: Borel sets agree with clopen sets modulo negligible sets.

Step 3. Every A in the von Neumann algebra that commutes appropriately with c (lies in its commutant) and satisfies EAE = A already lies in c. It is the element of C(k') supported there. So the corner E c E is the algebra C(k'). The rest of this sentence is illegible.

Step 4 (Conclusion). The restriction of T to c = C_0(M) is a positive linear form, finite on the relevant functions. Hence it is given by a positive Radon measure μ on M, with T(f) = ∫ f dμ for f ∈ C_0(M). That is: T restricted to a maximal abelian subalgebra is integration against a Radon measure.

Purpose. The next page uses this to define the spectral measure of a normal element A of b by ⟨φ, μ_A⟩ = T(φ(A)). It then defines the decreasing rearrangement φ_A of a positive element, Φ_A = ∫_0^t φ_A, Ψ_A = ∫_0^t log φ_A, and Δ_A = exp Ψ_A. This is the preparatory material for Grothendieck's Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'.
errors: The passage from |U_f| ≤ U_g ∈ b to U_f ∈ b needs b to be hereditary (or the polar decomposition U_f = V|U_f|). This is true for two-sided ideals in a von Neumann algebra but is left implicit.

The identification U_f = U_h with h ∈ C_0(M) needs c to be maximal abelian in the appropriate sense, so that the bounded Borel calculus of c that lands in b returns to c. The page does not argue this explicitly.
The existence of a clopen compact k' with U_{φ_k} = U_{φ_{k'}} uses the Stonean/hyperstonean structure of M. This is asserted without proof.

ideas.what: Hereditary property of trace ideals: domination by an element of the ideal implies membership; the bounded Borel functional calculus inside the ideal
ideas.modern_name: hereditary ideals / faces of a trace in a von Neumann algebra
ideas.where_published: possibly implicit in Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955)

ideas.what: A trace restricted to a maximal abelian subalgebra C_0(M) is a Radon measure on M
ideas.modern_name: restriction of a normal semifinite trace to a masa is a measure; spectral distribution of a normal operator w.r.t. a trace
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), spectral measure / rearrangement setup

ideas.what: Projections of characteristic functions of compact sets coincide with those of clopen compact sets
ideas.modern_name: hyperstonean spectrum of an abelian von Neumann algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dixmier 1951 (Sur certains espaces considérés par M. H. Stone)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine technical lemma in the preparation of Grothendieck's published 1955 Bourbaki exposé on rearrangements and convexity inequalities in von Neumann algebras with a trace. The measure-theoretic representation of a trace on a masa is standard (Dixmier, Segal), so nothing here appears to be missing from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'i.e. U_f est de 2 forme U_h' should read 'i.e. U_f est de la forme U_h'; likewise 'si f est de 2 forme φ_k' should read 'si f est de la forme φ_k'.
In the Step 3 sentence, 'Tout opérateur A dans 𝒜 qui appartient à c' probably reads 'qui permute à c' (commutes with c). The conclusion is that such A is in c, i.e. in C(k).
'𝓔(k)' is probably 'E c E' or 'C(k)', the corner algebra.
In the struck-out first line, 'les U_{φ_k} est dans b' probably reads 'les U_{φ_k} sont dans b'.
